why: Must_not item 1 is avoided. Check 3 goes through every function math.js exports and fails on "any exported function is MISSING", so a README that documents clamp but leaves out subtract fails. Checks 1, 2 and 4 are tied to behaviour and are not stricter than their lines. Check 2 accepts any RangeError, whatever its message. Item 2 is broken by Check 3, though. MISSING is decided by `r.includes(f+'(')`, and PASS requires "at minimum its name with its parameters". That makes the README use a particular form, with the name followed by "(" and its parameters. Expect line 3 only asks that each export be documented. A README that says "`subtract` — returns a minus b" documents the function but would be marked MISSING and FAIL. This is the kind of "specific README layout" requirement the must_not list rules out.
